niche: a regional health plan's 2027 in-home care contracts for its members aged 75 and over: the board's fixed home-care budget divided among seven regional home-care agencies in proportion to the members who lived in each agency's region for the greater part of 2025, each member's region conformed from the member file and the plan's own medical, pharmacy and laboratory claims, when members who spend the cooler months in the low desert keep their high-country address and high-country doctor on file
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads the agreement's residence clause, keeps the members aged 75 and over enrolled all year, places each in the region of the address on file (or of the plurality of primary care visits, the plan's own attribution rule, or of most of the year's claims) and divides the budget gives the high-country agencies the members who live in the low desert from October to May; reading each member's year from the dates and places of the claims moves those members and their share of the budget to the desert agencies.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each member's region of residence for the contract year, which health plans determine from the member file and the claims stream when they attribute members to regions and providers for capitation; put a school district's pupils and library loans in its place and there is no claim type, no mail-order pharmacy, no primary care attribution rule and no capitation contract, so the task stops reading.
layer1: medical claims from the plan's claims system with service dates and rendering provider NPIs, resubmitted claims carrying a frequency code and the original claim number, and denied lines left in the extract
pharmacy claims from the PBM's file with the pharmacy's NCPDP number, days supply and reversals, mail-order and specialty pharmacies located out of state
laboratory claims from the national laboratory vendor keyed by patient service centre
provider, pharmacy and draw-site registers each naming the region its own way (a county, a ZIP code, a service-centre code), with a 2025 practice relocation and an agency renamed
the member file's address history with notified dates and a region assigned from the ZIP code, ZIP codes that straddle two counties
dates in the claims system's YYYYMMDD and the PBM's MM/DD/YYYY
stakeholder_role: the plan's director of provider contracting and payment, who prepares the 2027 home-care allocation for the board

spine.entity: one adjudicated medical claim line: member, service date, rendering provider, place of service

world.geography: United States, Arizona (a fictional regional health plan, its seven home-care regions, agencies, providers and people are invented; counties, ZIP codes and the climate are real)
world.org_type: regional health plan with a seniors' managed-care product and contracted regional home-care agencies

driver: The decisive quantity is each member's place of residence over a year, defined as where the member lived for the greater part of it; the address on file and the place of most of the member's routine contacts both stay at a home the member leaves for most of the year, so the place is read from the dated places of every contact the member made, which run unbroken through the months spent elsewhere, rather than from the record's address, the contact count or the latest contact.
driver_concrete: Each member's 2025 region is where the plan's claims place them for most of the year: members who live from October to May in the low desert keep their high-country address and high-country doctor, whose summer visits, specialists and laboratory draws outnumber the desert's pharmacy fills and urgent care, but every desert month carries a desert claim, so only the claims' dates and places, read day by day, move them.
stump: A competent analyst places each member aged 75 and over in the region of the address on file at 31 December 2025, or of the plurality of primary care visits, and leaves the high-country agencies their snowbirds' share of the 2027 budget; the step that lands it there is taking the address or the doctor for the residence, when the claims' dates and places show those members living in the desert for most of 2025.

differentiation.task306: task306 v1 sized next year's refurbishment demand by the used imports still to arrive outside the current roll; here every member is on file and enrolled all year, nothing arrives, and the deciding step reads where each member lived from the dated places of their own claims rather than their address
differentiation.task468: task468 v2 and v3 priced a group's coming-year cost on how long each unit's current spell of activity had run; here no cost is projected and no spell length enters: each member's region for a closed year is read from where their claims fall day by day
differentiation.task247: task247 refilled a monitoring record's gap-filled days from the observations on both sides of each gap; here no record is missing or filled: the address on file is correct as the member's notified home, and the claims show where the member actually lived for most of the year

spine.entity: one monitored unit's operation in one clock hour
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of EPA's Clean Air Markets hourly emissions export)

world.geography: United States: Washington and Oregon (the Pacific Northwest)
world.org_type: a public utility district buying baseload capacity, the sellers' gas-fired plants, the state emissions performance standard
invented_names: Calder County Public Utility District No. 1

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a ratio of input to output that depends on the operating level, falling as output rises and rising again once a supplementary stage is engaged above a unit's base capability, so the ratio over a closed period reflects the levels the unit happened to run at; the decision commits each unit to one stated level in every interval, a level some units rarely held and others can reach only with the supplementary stage, so the ratio has to be read at that level from the interval records, not carried from the period average.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each offered gas unit's CO2 per net MWh under the baseload commitment is its rate at the contract capacity in every hour: cycling combined cycles whose 2024 and 2025 records are full of starts and part-load hours look above 925 pounds on their annual averages yet sit well under it at full output, while a base-loaded unit offered at a contract capacity above its unfired capability will run its duct burners in every contract hour and lands above 925 though its annual average is under it.
lineage.stump: The default path rates each offered plant on its 2025 annual pounds of CO2 per net MWh, which fails the cycling combined cycles Sorrel Butte, Kessling Creek and Ashby Gulch on their starts and part-load hours and passes Tamarack Landing, whose annual average is mostly unfired base operation, so the price-ordered fill takes Tamarack Landing and Moraine Point for 905 MW; read at each offer's contract capacity, the rate passes the three cycling plants and fails Tamarack Landing, offered at a capacity it reaches only with its duct burners firing in every hour, and the fill takes Juniper Draw, Kessling Creek and Ashby Gulch for 990 MW.
